name: Nice & the Riviera
tagline: Belle Époque glamour along the azure Mediterranean coast.
bestMonths: May, Jun, Jul, Aug and Sep
whenBlurb: Warm sea and calmer crowds in late spring and September; February brings Carnival and citrus. July-August is hot, brilliant and busy.

ourTake.lede: Nice is the right base for the Riviera, better value and more real life than Cannes or Monaco, and everything is a short train ride away. Skip the pebble beach for the old town and the Cimiez hills; the daily Cours Saleya market and a Niçoise lunch beat any beach club. Use the coastal train as your car: Villefranche, Èze and Menton are all quick hops, and the corniche drives are the day out worth renting for.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the Riviera: the sea, the light, and Monaco and Cannes at hand.
ourTake.skipIf: You want budget or solitude; this coast trades on glamour and it prices accordingly.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc
items.description: The legend of the Riviera since 1870, a white palace on its own cape, with the sea-cut Eden-Roc pool the coast's most famous set piece.

items.name: Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat, A Four Seasons Hotel
items.description: A Belle Époque palace on seven hectares at the tip of the coast's most exclusive cape, private, forested and utterly serene.

items.name: Château de la Chèvre d'Or
items.description: A medieval eyrie clinging to the cliff of Èze village, 400m above the sea, the Riviera's most romantic address, with two-starred dining in-house.

items.name: La Réserve de Beaulieu & Spa
items.description: A rose-pink Italianate villa on its own harbour since 1880, a hushed, aristocratic grande dame between Nice and Monaco.

items.name: Hôtel de Paris Monte-Carlo
items.description: The 1864 palace of the Place du Casino, the founding grand hotel of Monte-Carlo, home to Ducasse's three-star Le Louis XV.

items.name: Cap Estel
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A private peninsula of five acres between Nice and Monaco, a villa hotel wrapped by the sea on three sides, screened from the world.

items.name: Le Negresco
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Nice's own pink-domed palace on the Promenade des Anglais, a private, family-owned house of art and theatre, a national monument since 1974.

items.name: Anantara Plaza Nice Hotel
items.description: An 1848 Belle Époque landmark off the Promenade, reborn by Anantara, Nice's most polished contemporary luxury, with a rooftop over the old town.

items.name: Hôtel Martinez, Cannes (Hyatt Unbound Collection)
items.description: The Art Deco grande dame of the Croisette, the address of the Film Festival, with the largest private beach in Cannes and a starred kitchen.

items.name: Hôtel Barrière Le Majestic Cannes
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A white 1926 palace at the head of the Croisette, grand, gracious and at the very centre of Cannes' glamour.

items.name: Promenade des Anglais
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera
items.description: The seven-kilometre Belle Époque seafront curving along the Baie des Anges, its blue chairs facing the water and the ochre Négresco dome behind. An unhurried morning stroll here, ice-cream in hand, is the Riviera at its most effortless, perfect for three generations moving at their own pace.

items.name: Vieux Nice (Old Town)
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera
items.description: A warren of ochre-and-terracotta lanes, baroque churches and shaded piazzas where laundry strings hang above artisan gelato shops. This is the emotional heart of Nice, small enough to wander with children, layered enough to reward a return each evening for aperitivo.

items.name: Cours Saleya Market
items.description: The famous flower-and-produce market, cut peonies, Menton lemons, tapenade, socca fresh off the copper pan, with a Monday antiques market in place of flowers. A vivid morning for the family, and a generous window into Niçoise produce for veg-leaning palates.

items.name: Colline du Château (Castle Hill)
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera
items.description: The green headland between the old town and the port, crowned by a man-made waterfall and the definitive view down over the terracotta rooftops and the sweep of the Baie des Anges. Reachable by a discreet free lift for those who prefer not to climb.

items.name: Musée Matisse
items.description: A red-ochre Genoese villa set in an olive grove, holding one of the world's most complete Matisse collections, the artist lived and died in Nice and is buried nearby. Intimate, sunlit and rarely crowded, it pairs naturally with a picnic under the Cimiez olive trees.

items.name: Musée National Marc Chagall
items.description: Purpose-built to hold Chagall's luminous Biblical Message cycle, seventeen large canvases glowing in a calm, light-filled space he helped design. A short, deeply moving visit that lands equally with art lovers and first-timers.

items.name: MAMAC, Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
items.description: A striking marble-clad building holding Nice's own School (Yves Klein, Arman, the Nouveaux Réalistes) plus Warhol and Lichtenstein, with a rooftop terrace looking over the city. The contemporary counterweight to the city's Belle Époque grandeur.

items.name: Cimiez Quarter & Roman Ruins
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera
items.description: The genteel hill district of grand winter-palace hotels turned apartments, with Roman baths, an amphitheatre and a Franciscan monastery garden overlooking the coast. The refined, residential Nice the aristocracy chose, best explored slowly.

items.name: Port Lympia (Old Port)
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera
items.description: The photogenic old harbour framed by tall Italianate façades, where fishing boats sit beside superyachts and the seafood restaurants of the quai spill onto the water. The natural place to board a private charter or dine facing the masts at dusk.

items.name: Place Masséna & Promenade du Paillon
items.description: The grand red-arcaded square with its checkerboard paving and mirror-fountain, opening onto a long green park of water jets and lawns that runs to the sea. A cooling, kid-friendly spine through the city on hot afternoons.

items.name: Monaco & Monte-Carlo
items.description: The gilded sovereign city-state fifteen minutes along the coast, palace, harbour of superyachts, Belle Époque casino and grand hotels stacked on a rock over the sea. The Riviera's concentrated shot of glamour, best done by private driver for a day.

items.name: Casino de Monte-Carlo
items.description: Charles Garnier's Belle Époque temple of gaming, all gilt, marble and painted ceilings, facing the manicured casino gardens. Even without a chip on the table, the salons and the Café de Paris terrace opposite are pure theatre, jacket and passport advised.

items.name: Prince's Palace of Monaco
items.description: The Grimaldi family's residence high on the Rock, with lavish State Apartments open in season and the daily changing of the guard at 11:55 in the square outside. History and pageantry with one of the best harbour views in the principality.

items.name: Oceanographic Museum of Monaco
items.description: A monumental institution founded by Prince Albert I, clinging to the cliff eighty-five metres above the sea, with grand aquaria, a shark lagoon and a rooftop terrace. Genuinely spellbinding for children and a serene stop for adults.

items.name: The Monaco Grand Prix Circuit
items.description: The legendary street circuit runs through the everyday town, the Casino square, the Fairmont hairpin, the tunnel, the harbour chicane. Trace it on foot any day of the year, or watch it come alive over the late-May race weekend from a harbourside berth.

items.name: Èze Village
items.description: A medieval eagle's-nest village of stone lanes coiling up to a garden balcony 400 metres above the sea, entirely pedestrian and full of artisans' ateliers. One of the Riviera's most romantic vantage points, and a natural lunch stop between Nice and Monaco.

items.name: Jardin Exotique d'Èze
items.description: A cascade of cacti and succulents crowning the ruined castle at the very top of Èze, opening onto a dizzying panorama that on clear days reaches to Corsica. Small, sculptural and quietly the finest view in the village.

items.name: Sentier Nietzsche
items.description: The steep zig-zag path linking the seaside to the perched village, walked by the philosopher who is said to have drawn inspiration here. A vigorous, scented climb for the energetic, or an easy downhill after a private car drops you at the top.

items.name: Villefranche-sur-Mer
items.description: A jewel-box fishing port on one of the Mediterranean's deepest natural harbours, with a rose-and-ochre old town, a Cocteau-painted chapel and a sheltered beach. Ten minutes from Nice yet a world softer, a favourite anchorage for private yachts.

items.name: Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat
items.description: The discreet green peninsula of billionaires' villas and pine-shaded coastal paths, with a low-key port and some of the most exclusive addresses on the coast. Precisely the kind of quiet, moneyed seclusion the Riviera's oldest fortunes prize.

items.name: Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild
items.description: Baroness Béatrice de Rothschild's rose-pink palace on the crest of Cap Ferrat, ringed by nine themed gardens, French, Spanish, Florentine, Japanese, around a musical fountain. The Riviera's most exquisite house-and-garden day, and candlelit on summer evenings.

items.name: Villa Kérylos
items.description: A faithful recreation of an ancient Greek villa built on a rocky point over the sea by archaeologist Théodore Reinach, complete with mosaics, frescoes and Antiquity-inspired furniture. A serene, scholarly counterpoint to the coast's Belle Époque excess.

items.name: Antibes Old Town & Marché Provençal
items.description: Ramparts against the sea, cobbled lanes and a superb covered Provençal market of cheeses, olives, flowers and produce. Antibes wears its history lightly and dines beautifully, an easy, atmospheric half-day with the family.

items.name: Musée Picasso, Antibes
items.description: Set in the seafront Château Grimaldi where Picasso worked for a joyous few months in 1946, holding the paintings and ceramics he left behind. Compact, sunlit and looking straight onto the Mediterranean that fills the canvases.

items.name: Cap d'Antibes & Sentier du Littoral
items.description: The legendary green cape of grand villas and the fabled Eden-Roc, ringed by a coastal footpath past secret coves and the so-called Billionaires' Bay. Old-money glamour at its most photographed, walk the path, then a private lunch behind the pines.

items.name: Port Vauban & the Superyacht Quay
items.description: One of the Mediterranean's largest marinas, its 'Quai des Milliardaires' berthing the world's most extraordinary superyachts beneath the old fort. A striking evening walk, and the practical launch point for a day at sea.

items.name: Cannes, La Croisette
items.description: The palm-lined boulevard of palace hotels, designer flagships and private beach clubs where the film festival unfurls its red carpet each May. Glamour worn openly, dress the part and take an evening promenade past the Carlton and Martinez.

items.name: Le Suquet, Old Cannes
items.description: The steep original village above the port, its stepped lanes climbing to a watchtower and a panorama over the bay. A far quieter, more soulful Cannes than the Croisette, best at golden hour before dinner on the Rue Saint-Antoine.

items.name: Île Sainte-Marguerite
items.description: A short boat hop from Cannes to a pine-and-eucalyptus island of turquoise coves, ringed by the Fort Royal that once held the Man in the Iron Mask. Swim, walk and picnic where the crowds thin, bring a private tender for the finest anchorages.

items.name: Île Saint-Honorat & Lérins Abbey
items.description: A tiny monastic island farmed by Cistercian monks who make the celebrated Lérins wines and liqueurs among the vines and chapels. A rare, contemplative escape ten minutes from the glitz, tastings and a fortified monastery to explore.

items.name: Saint-Paul-de-Vence
items.description: A ravishing fortified hill village of galleries and stone ramparts that drew Chagall, Signac and half of mid-century Paris; Chagall is buried in its cemetery. Wander the lanes, then lunch at the storied La Colombe d'Or among its Picassos and Mirós.

items.name: Fondation Maeght
items.description: One of Europe's great private art foundations, a modernist building set in pine woods with a Giacometti courtyard, a Miró labyrinth and Braque pools, freshly expanded for its 60th anniversary. A pilgrimage for anyone serious about 20th-century art.

items.name: Grasse, Perfume Capital
items.description: The inland town that has scented the world for centuries, where the historic houses of Fragonard, Galimard and Molinard open their workshops. Compose your own bespoke fragrance in a private atelier, an intimate, memorable family afternoon.

items.name: Menton
items.description: The last town before Italy, a pastel amphitheatre of lemon groves and gardens basking in the Riviera's mildest microclimate, host to the famous February Lemon Festival. Softly Italianate and blissfully unhurried, a gentle day for all generations.

items.name: Jardin Serre de la Madone & Menton's Gardens
items.description: Menton's exceptional climate nurtures a constellation of botanical gardens, the terraced Serre de la Madone, the exotic Val Rahmeh, the Fontana Rosa. A tranquil, fragrant counterpoint for garden lovers away from the beach crowds.

items.name: The Three Corniches Drive
items.description: Three tiered clifftop roads, Basse, Moyenne and the vertiginous Grande Corniche, thread between Nice and Menton past Èze and Roquebrune with staggering sea views. The Riviera's definitive drive, best savoured slowly from the back of a private car.

items.name: Gorges du Verdon
items.description: Europe's grandest canyon, where turquoise water winds between limestone walls hundreds of metres deep, opening onto the emerald Lac de Sainte-Croix. A dramatic full-day inland expedition of clifftop drives, kayaking and the lavender plateaux beyond.

items.name: Roquebrune-Cap-Martin
items.description: A medieval hill village crowned by one of France's oldest castle keeps, with a coastal cape below of villas, pines and Le Corbusier's tiny Cabanon. Quiet, storied and perched between Monaco and Menton, a graceful hour or two off the main track.

items.name: Beaches & Private Beach Clubs of Nice
items.description: Along the Baie des Anges, a run of managed beach clubs offer loungers, umbrellas and service on the famous pebble shore, from Blue Beach to the hotel-run establishments. Reserve a front-row set, the discreet way to enjoy the sea in comfort.

items.name: Plage de Paloma & Cap Ferrat Coves
items.description: The elegant crescent of Paloma Beach on the tip of Cap Ferrat, with its long-loved beach restaurant and clear, sheltered water. The insiders' choice for a refined, uncrowded swim reached by coastal path or private tender.

items.name: Pampelonne-style Days at Juan-les-Pins
items.description: The lively pine-fringed bay next to Cap d'Antibes, birthplace of Riviera beach glamour in the Jazz Age and still lined with sandy beach clubs and evening bars. A more animated, youthful counterpoint for the family's beach day.

items.name: Private Yacht Charter along the Coast
items.description: The truest way to experience the Côte d'Azur, cast off from Nice, Antibes or Cannes to anchor off Cap Ferrat, the Lérins islands and the coves of Cap d'Antibes for a swim and lunch aboard. Privacy, freedom and the coast seen from its best angle.

items.name: Socca & Niçoise Table
items.description: Nice has its own cuisine, chickpea socca hot off the griddle, pan bagnat, ratatouille, tender-veg tians and pissaladière, much of it naturally vegetable-led. Graze the old town's institutions, or arrange a private Niçoise tasting for the family.

items.name: Vence & the Chapelle du Rosaire (Matisse Chapel)
items.description: A walled town near Saint-Paul whose true treasure is the little Rosary Chapel that Matisse designed and considered his masterpiece, pure white walls lit by cobalt-and-gold glass. A quiet, luminous stop for those who love him.

items.name: Mougins, Hilltop Village of Gastronomy
items.description: A pristine spiral village above Cannes where Picasso spent his last years, now a haven of galleries and celebrated tables. A polished, art-and-food afternoon away from the coast, easily paired with Grasse.

items.name: Musée Jean Cocteau, Menton
items.description: Menton's tribute to the poet-artist Jean Cocteau, spanning the little seafront Bastion he decorated himself and the collection he left the town. A charming, human-scaled museum to close a slow day near the Italian border.

items.name: Mirazur
items.description: Mauro Colagreco's cliff-garden temple above the Italian border, seed-to-plate cooking from twelve acres of biodynamic terraces, once the best restaurant on earth.

items.name: Le Louis XV-Alain Ducasse
items.description: Ducasse's landmark of Mediterranean 'naturalité' in the Hôtel de Paris, a founding three-star of the modern Riviera.

items.name: La Chèvre d'Or
items.description: Two-starred cooking suspended on the cliff of Èze village, the whole coast falling away below, chef Tom Meyer, Meilleur Ouvrier de France.

items.name: Flaveur
items.description: The Tourteaux brothers' two-star in central Nice, bold, spice-laced Mediterranean cooking, with Indian notes woven through local seafood.

items.name: La Palme d'Or
items.description: The Art Deco fine-dining room of the Hôtel Martinez, relaunched under Jean Imbert, the star table of the Croisette.

items.name: Le Restaurant des Rois
items.description: Julien Roucheteau's gastronomic room at La Réserve de Beaulieu, haute cuisine in a sumptuous seafront salon.

items.name: Le Chantecler
items.description: The starred dining room of Le Negresco, Virginie Basselot, Meilleur Ouvrier de France, cooking Mediterranean haute gastronomie in a wood-panelled salon.

items.name: Louroc
items.description: The starred restaurant of Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc, sea-facing Mediterranean cooking at the Riviera's most legendary address.

items.name: JAN
items.description: Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen's intimate 20-seater near the port, French technique threaded with a South African soul.

items.name: Pure & V
items.description: Chef Pinja Paakkonen's Nordic-inflected kitchen in central Nice, with one of the coast's most characterful natural-wine lists.

items.name: Racines - Bruno Cirino
items.description: Bruno Cirino's 'kitchen-garden cuisine', a single set menu of perfectly-ripe Mediterranean produce, largely vegetarian and farm-driven.

items.name: L'Aromate
items.description: Mickaël Gracieux's refined, produce-driven cooking in the heart of Nice, a quietly serious one-star.

items.name: Peixes
items.description: Fish and seafood served tapas-style in a blue-and-white tiled bistro near the opera, vibrant, Mediterranean-meets-South-American, and much loved.

items.name: Le Bistrot de Jan
items.description: The relaxed sibling of starred JAN, the same South African-French spirit at an easier, everyday pitch.

items.name: Maison Barale
items.description: A century-old Niçois family kitchen in Vieux Nice, the real ravioli, daube and socca of the old town.

items.name: La Merenda
credentials: A celebrated Niçois institution, chef Dominique Le Stanc (ex-Le Chantecler ★★)
items.description: Dominique Le Stanc's tiny, cash-only Niçoise counter, a former two-star chef cooking the humble classics of Nice by hand.

items.name: Le Relais
credentials: Within Le Negresco, Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Le Negresco's walnut-panelled bar since 1913, a century of Riviera legend from Delon to the Beatles, hushed by day, jazz-lit by night.

items.name: Le Bar Américain, Hôtel de Paris Monte-Carlo
credentials: Within Hôtel de Paris Monte-Carlo, Société des Bains de Mer
items.description: A wood-and-brass grand-hotel bar off the Place du Casino, live piano and the old glamour of Monte-Carlo.

items.name: Le Bar Churchill, Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc
credentials: Within Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc, MICHELIN Key (2025), Oetker Collection
items.description: The clubby bar of the Riviera's most legendary hotel, a Negroni among the pines, where the coast's glamour has gathered for a century.

items.name: Bar du Cap, Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat
credentials: Within Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat, A Four Seasons Hotel, MICHELIN Key (2025)
items.description: An elegant, low-lit bar in a Four Seasons palace on the cape, quiet, grown-up and framed by seven hectares of garden.

items.name: Le Bar du Ciel, Anantara Plaza Nice
credentials: Within Anantara Plaza Nice, MICHELIN Guide Hotel (Selected)
items.description: A rooftop bar over the old town and the sea, cocktails at golden hour above the centre of Nice.

items.name: Buddha-Bar Monte-Carlo
credentials: Part of the global Buddha-Bar name
items.description: A former concert hall turned Asian-themed temple of DJs and late nights, the loud, glamorous centre of Monaco's after-dark.

items.name: Movida / Vieux Nice bar quarter
items.description: The lanes around the Cours Saleya and Rue de la Préfecture, where Nice's own late night gathers, spilling from bar to bar.

plan.heading: 5 days on the Riviera, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle in at the Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat, then the coastal path around the peninsula.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild and its nine gardens above the sea.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Le Cap, the hotel's Michelin table, with the terrace open to the bay.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The flower market on Cours Saleya, then the Musée Matisse in Cimiez.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Promenade des Anglais and the old town's ochre lanes at leisure.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Le Chantecler at the Negresco, a grande dame's dining room.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive the Grande Corniche to the perched village of Èze and its exotic garden.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Down to Monaco for the old town and the Oceanographic Museum.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Le Louis XV, Alain Ducasse at the Hôtel de Paris, Monte-Carlo.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Musée Picasso in the Château Grimaldi at Antibes, above the ramparts.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A boat along the Cap d'Antibes, lunch at Eden-Roc if the season allows.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A quiet dinner back on Cap-Ferrat, the water at your feet.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Inland to the Fondation Maeght for the Giacomettis and the Miró garden.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The ramparts of Saint-Paul-de-Vence, then Matisse's Chapelle du Rosaire in Vence.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at La Colombe d'Or, the artists' inn, its walls hung with the payment.

items.name: Vieux Nice
items.description: The atmospheric old town of markets and narrow lanes; lively and central, best for first visits.

items.name: Cimiez
items.description: Leafy hillside of Belle Époque villas and Roman ruins; quiet and residential, for a calmer stay.

items.name: Le Port / Riquier
items.description: Around the harbour, with the best local dining and fewer tourists; for those who want neighbourhood life.

events.name: Nice Carnival
events.note: One of the world's great carnivals, with flower battles and huge floats along the Promenade des Anglais.

events.name: Fête du Citron (Menton Lemon Festival)
events.note: Giant sculptures built from citrus fruit in nearby Menton, a short train ride east.

events.name: Nice Jazz Fest
events.note: A summer institution of over 70 years, staged in the heart of the city.

events.name: Jazz à Juan (Juan-les-Pins)
events.note: The legendary seaside jazz festival along the coast at Antibes.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Cap-Ferrat and Cap d'Antibes are the discreet places to stay; July and August are crowded and yachts and villas are reserved months ahead, and evenings on the coast run late and relaxed rather than formal.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Nice Cote d'Azur; a seven-minute helicopter transfer reaches Monaco, or a chauffeured car runs the coast road to Cap-Ferrat, Antibes or Saint-Tropez.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver for the corniches and coastal villages, with a chartered yacht or tender the natural way to move along the water in season.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Strong along the coast; a French eSIM covers the whole Riviera, and villas and hotels offer good wifi.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Euro (Monaco uses it too); cards are universal and service is included, so tipping is modest and optional.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: May-June and September give warm sea, calm light and the coast before and after the crush. July-August is beautiful but crowded and hot; November-March is quiet and many finer addresses close.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No nonstop from India; cleanest routing is direct to Paris on Air France, then a 1.5-hour hop to Nice, or via a Gulf hub (Emirates, Qatar Qsuite) or London. For a seamless arrival, hold business through to Nice on one ticket and pre-arrange a car from the terminal along the Basse Corniche.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required; very safe. Normal care with valuables in Nice old town and Cannes at events. Tap water is potable across the Riviera.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian is manageable but not a regional strength; Jain and no-onion-garlic need advance notice at most kitchens. Indian food is limited outside Nice and Monaco, so a villa chef briefed on veg/Jain is the reliable route; Monte-Carlo's hotel dining will cater on request.
